chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There used to be for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) a musk holder. Whenever he performed ablution, he would take it in his hand while it was wet. So when he went out, they would recognize that he was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) by its fragrance.

key_terms.رَطْبَةٌ: Wet (referring to the hand or the musk)
key_terms.مَمْسَكَةٌ: A container or holder for musk

ai.seo_question: How did people recognize the Prophet Muhammad by his scent after ablution?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, this narration highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) use of musk as a sign of purity and distinctiveness, linking physical fragrance to spiritual presence. Scholars note that the musk container (*mamsakah*) served as a practical identifier for his followers, reflecting the cultural significance of scent in 7th-century Arabia. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s tangible, sensory attributes as part of his prophetic identity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There used to be for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> a musk holder. Whenever he<sup>saww</sup> performed ablution, he<sup>saww</sup> would grab it with his<sup>saww</sup> hands while wet. So when he<sup>saww</sup> went out, it would be recognised that he<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> by its fragrance’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had a musk container. When making wudu he would take it in his hand while wet. When coming out people noticed his coming because of the perfume and fragrance.’”
